summary: Defines a YANG data model that augments the IETF OSPF YANG model (RFC 9129) to support OSPFv3 Extended Link State Advertisements (RFC 8362). Extended LSAs use extensible TLV-based formats for the base LSA types of RFC 5340.

plainLanguage.summary: A YANG model is a form for configuring network gear. This adds form fields for the newer, more flexible announcements of OSPFv3.

questions: what is the ospfv3 extended lsa yang model
how to enable ospfv3 extended lsa support
subtitle: The YANG model that lets management tools switch on and inspect OSPFv3 Extended LSAs.

tldr.problem: OSPFv3 Extended LSAs (RFC 8362) carry routing data as extensible TLVs, but there was no standard YANG data model to configure them or to read them from a router's link state database.
tldr.mechanism: The module ietf-ospfv3-extended-lsa augments the OSPF YANG model of RFC 9129 with a switch for Extended LSA support at the OSPF instance and area level, plus read-only nodes for each Extended LSA type in the database.
tldr.outcome: Operators and tools can manage OSPFv3 Extended LSAs through NETCONF or RESTCONF using one vendor-neutral schema.

today: RFC 9587 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2024, and the data supplied for this RFC lists no obsoleting or updating documents. It is the YANG module that accompanies RFC 8362 and builds on RFC 9129.

sections.title: What This Module Is For
sections.content:
YANG is a data definition language used to define the contents of a conceptual datastore, which lets networked devices be managed using NETCONF. This document defines a YANG data model that augments the IETF OSPF YANG data model of RFC 9129, which itself augments the routing model of RFC 8349.

The model provides configuration and operational state for OSPFv3 Extended Link State Advertisements (LSAs), defined in RFC 8362. Extended LSAs are extensible, TLV-based LSAs for the base LSA types defined in RFC 5340. The module conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA) of RFC 8342, and the tree diagrams use the notation of RFC 8340.
sections.plainLanguage: Routers speak a language called OSPFv3 to tell each other about the network. This document writes down a standard form for controlling and reading one newer part of that language.

sections.title: How the Module Fits In
sections.content:
The Extended LSA module requires support for the OSPF base model, which defines basic OSPF configuration and state. The augmentations in the ietf-ospfv3-extended-lsa module provide three things: global configuration, area configuration, and the addition of OSPFv3 Extended LSAs to the Link State Database (LSDB) operational state.

The module uses prefix ospfv3-e-lsa and the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-ospfv3-extended-lsa. It imports the routing, OSPF, inet and routing-types modules, and its first revision is dated 2024-06-07.
sections.plainLanguage: It is an add-on, like a new attachment for a tool you already own. It only works together with the existing OSPF model.

sections.title: Configuration: Extended LSA Support
sections.content:
The configurable part is small. A boolean leaf extended-lsa-support is added in two places: under the OSPF instance (global) and under each area. These are the only writable nodes the module adds.

The Security Considerations explain why the switch is sensitive: OSPFv3 routers use solely OSPFv3 Extended LSAs or OSPFv3 Legacy LSAs for the SPF computation. Routers using different types of LSAs result in incomplete reachability and possible partitioning of the routing domain. The RFC points to Section 6 of RFC 8362 for Extended LSA compatibility.
sections.plainLanguage: There is one on/off switch, and it can be set for the whole router or for one area. If neighbors disagree about the switch, they stop understanding each other.

sections.title: Operational State: Extended LSAs in the LSDB
sections.content:
The rest of the module is read-only (ro) state added to the LSDB. Each Extended LSA type gets its own container, which applies only when the LSA header type matches:

  • e-link (link scope): router priority, LSA options and a list of TLVs.
  • e-router, e-network, e-inter-area-prefix, e-inter-area-router, e-intra-area-prefix and e-nssa (area scope).
  • e-as-external (AS scope).

Every list of TLVs can hold an unknown-tlv entry with a type, a length and a hex-string value, so TLVs the model does not know can still be shown. Known TLVs such as the intra-area prefix, link, attached-router and external-prefix TLVs expose fields like metric, prefix, prefix options and neighbor router IDs, and many carry sub-TLV lists. The external-prefix TLV has forwarding-address and route-tag sub-TLVs.

The module also defines identities for each Extended LSA type and for prefix option bits (such as nu-bit, la-bit, p-bit, dn-bit and n-bit) and the external e-bit.
sections.plainLanguage: Beyond the switch, the model adds labeled slots on the router's notice board, one kind for each type of announcement, plus a catch-all slot for announcements nobody has a name for yet.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The data is designed to be accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF. NETCONF's mandatory-to-implement secure transport is Secure Shell (SSH), and RESTCONF's is TLS over HTTPS. The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) of RFC 8341 can restrict which users reach which operations and content.

Writing the two extended-lsa-support nodes without protection can cause a denial-of-service attack. Reading is sensitive too: exposing the LSDB exposes the detailed topology of the network, including topology learned from other routers, which may facilitate other attacks and which operators may regard as confidential.
sections.plainLanguage: Only trusted people should be allowed to flip the switch, and only trusted people should read the notice board, because it is a map of the whole network.

sections.title: Configuration Example
sections.content: Appendix A shows the same configuration in XML and in JSON (RFC 7951). It sets up a routing instance with router ID 192.0.2.1 and a control-plane protocol of type ospf:ospfv3 named "OSPFv3", then sets extended-lsa-support to true under the OSPF instance.
sections.plainLanguage: The appendix shows a filled-in form where the one new switch is turned on.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-ospfv3-extended-lsa in the IETF XML Registry. It also registered the YANG module ietf-ospfv3-extended-lsa in the YANG Module Names registry, with prefix ospfv3-e-lsa and reference RFC 9587.
sections.plainLanguage: The official name list now includes this module, so no one else can claim its name.
